title: get_file_contents says encoding base64 after content is already decoded
claim: Through @modelcontextprotocol/server-github, get_file_contents returns encoding:"base64" while content is already UTF-8 text. Trusting the field and decoding again corrupts a file you already hold.
appliesTo: Crew GitHub door wrapping @modelcontextprotocol/server-github (stdio). Observed 2026-09-12 on private fantasyb/jeevz text files.
reflexBecause: A plain "decode when labeled base64" reflex is exactly what corrupts the payload; the trap is the field lying after the server already decoded, which is not recoverable by retry or pagination.
expectation: encoding:"base64" means content is base64 and must be decoded — same contract as the GitHub Contents API.
reality: On fantasyb/jeevz package.json through the Cairn GitHub door: encoding was "base64" but content already started with printable JSON. Parsing content as UTF-8 works; base64-decoding it yields garbage. Raw gh api Contents still returns true base64 — the MCP layer decoded and left the lying label.
mechanism: The MCP server decodes text payloads for the model but forwards the upstream metadata object including encoding:"base64", so the label describes the API wire form, not the bytes in content.
workaround: Do not base64-decode solely because encoding says base64. Use content as text first (parse JSON / printable ASCII). Decode only when content looks like base64 and fails as text.

evidence.command: Through crew/client-mcp.json (cairn-proxy --config crew/github-door.json), CAIRN_AGENT=Dig: get_file_contents owner=fantasyb repo=jeevz path=package.json
evidence.output: encoding_field=base64; content already printable JSON; content_is_valid_json=true; base64_decode_of_content_is_valid_json=false
evidence.note: Door session dig-earn / dig-b64; ledger get_file_contents [args: owner, path, repo].

evidence.output: encoding=base64; content_prefix is true base64 on the raw Contents API
evidence.note: Shows the MCP layer, not GitHub, is what returns decoded content under a base64 label.

check.command: Call get_file_contents on a known small JSON file through the GitHub door; if encoding is base64 and content already parses as JSON without decoding, the trap still holds. If content is true base64 (decoding yields the JSON), the trap is gone.
check.confirmedIf: encoding is base64 AND content parses as the file without base64 decode AND base64-decoding content does not yield the file
check.refutedIf: content is actual base64 matching the Contents API (decode yields the file) or encoding is utf-8/omitted to match the bytes returned

observations.note: Recorded at the moment it was solved; no note was supplied.

environment.note: Linux 6.12.94+; the machine that recorded it — the submitter reported no environment
